name: 12-Item Scale for Depressive Mixed State (DMX-12)
description: A 12-item self-rating questionnaire assessing depressive mixed state (DMX) symptoms over the past week. Each item is rated 0-3 by frequency. A total score sums all 12 items; a screening subscore sums 8 discriminative items (screen positive at >=13). Higher scores indicate greater severity of depressive mixed features.
citation: Shinzato H, Koda M, Nakamura A, Kondo T (2019). Development of the 12-item questionnaire for quantitative assessment of depressive mixed state (DMX-12). Neuropsychiatric Disease and Treatment, 15, 1983-1991. https://doi.org/10.2147/NDT.S215478

name: 3-Item Care Transition Measure (CTM-3)
description: 3-item patient-reported measure of the quality of preparation for hospital discharge (care transition), covering shared decision-making, understanding of self-management responsibilities, and understanding of medication purpose. A component of the HCAHPS survey (NQF #0228) used in U.S. Medicare/CMS quality programs. Items are scored to a 0-100 scale; higher = better care-transition quality.
citation: Coleman, E. A., Mahoney, E., & Parry, C. (2005). Assessing the quality of preparation for posthospital care from the patient's perspective: the Care Transitions Measure. Medical Care, 43(3), 246-255. https://doi.org/10.1097/00005650-200503000-00007
license: Free to use with attribution (© Eric A. Coleman, MD, MPH)

name: Ability to Integrate Beauty Scale (AIBS)
description: A single-factor, 7-item self-report scale measuring the ability to integrate beauty (AIB), i.e., the capacity to change one's thinking and undergo inner transformation as a result of aesthetic experiences. Items are rated on a 1-7 scale and summed; higher scores indicate a greater ability to integrate beauty.
citation: Swiatek, A. H., & Szczesniak, M. (2023). The Ability to Integrate Beauty Scale (AIBS): Construction and Psychometric Properties on a Scale for Measuring Aesthetic Intelligence as a Resource for Personal Development. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 16, 1647-1662. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S407553

name: Acceptance Scale for Traditional Chinese Medicine Techniques in Cancer Patients (TCM-AS)
description: A 25-item measure of cancer patients' acceptance of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) techniques, based on the Technology Acceptance Model. Four dimensions: Perceived Usefulness, Perceived Ease of Use, Behavioral Intention, and Apprehensions About Usage. Each dimension uses a 5-point scale whose anchors are pre-calibrated so that a higher score always indicates greater acceptance; items are summed (range 25-125).
citation: Yang, L., Sheng, X., Lin, J., et al. (2025). Acceptance Scale for Traditional Chinese Medicine Techniques in Cancer Patients: Development and Validation. Patient Preference and Adherence, 19, 1-16. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S550541

name: Adult Autism Spectrum Quotient (AQ)
description: A 50-item self-administered instrument for measuring the degree to which an adult with normal intelligence has the traits associated with the autistic spectrum. The 50 questions are made up of 10 questions assessing five different areas: - social skill (items 1, 11, 13, 15, 22, 36, 44, 45, 47, 48); - attention switching (items 2, 4, 10, 16, 25, 32, 34, 37, 43, 46); - attention to detail (items 5, 6, 9, 12, 19, 23, 28, 29, 30, 49); - communication (items 7, 17, 18, 26, 27, 31, 33, 35, 38, 39); -
citation: Cohen S, Wheelwright S, Skinner R, Martin J, Clubley E (2001). The autism-spectrum quotient (AQ): evidence from Asperger syndrome/high-functioning autism, males and females, scientists and mathematicians. *J Autism Dev Disord.* 31(1): 5-17. Erratum in: *J Autism Dev Disord.* 2001 Dec;31(6):603. https://doi.org/10.1023/a:1005653411471 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11439754/

name: Affective Dependence Scale (ADS-9)
description: A 9-item self-report measure of affective (emotional) dependence in intimate relationships, with two subscales: Submission (adaptation, accommodation, and subjugation to the partner) and Craving (imperious need of the partner accompanied by disturbing states). Items are rated on a 5-point agreement scale; subscale and total scores are the mean of their items, with higher scores indicating greater affective dependence.
citation: Sirvent-Ruiz CM, Moral-Jimenez MV, Herrero J, Miranda-Roves M, Rodriguez Diaz FJ (2022). Concept of Affective Dependence and Validation of an Affective Dependence Scale. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 15, 3875-3888. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S385807

name: Agricultural Safety and Health Literacy Tool (ASHL)
description: A 22-item self-report tool measuring agricultural safety and health literacy across five subscales: Access (5), Understanding (5), Appraise (4), Apply (4), and Attitude (4). Items are rated on a 4-point agreement scale and summed; higher scores indicate higher agricultural safety and health literacy.
citation: Lee GY, Park KS (2025). Development and Validation of an Agricultural Safety and Health Literacy Tool. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 18, 4059-4070. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S528979

name: ALGA-Breast Cancer Patient-Profiling Questionnaire (ALGA-BC)
description: A 29-item multidimensional questionnaire profiling breast cancer patients across eight factors: Global Self-Rated Health, Perceived Physical Health, Anxiety, Self-Efficacy, Cognitive Closure, Memory, Body Image, and Sexual Life. Each factor is scored as the mean of its items (after reverse-coding where indicated); higher factor scores indicate worse health/more symptoms.
citation: Gorini A, Mazzocco K, Gandini S, Munzone E, McVie G, Pravettoni G (2015). Development and psychometric testing of a breast cancer patient-profiling questionnaire. Breast Cancer: Targets and Therapy, 7, 133-146. https://doi.org/10.2147/BCTT.S80014

name: Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale
description: 21-item measure of anxiety toward artificial intelligence (Wang & Wang), with four factors: Learning (8 items), Job Replacement (6 items), Sociotechnical Blindness (4 items), and AI Configuration (3 items). Items are rated 1-7; subscales are averaged and the total is summed (21-147), with higher scores indicating greater AI anxiety. Includes the original English and a validated German translation.
citation: Wang, Y.-Y., & Wang, Y.-S. (2022). Development and validation of an artificial intelligence anxiety scale: An initial application in predicting motivated learning behavior. Interactive Learning Environments, 30(4), 619-634. https://doi.org/10.1080/10494820.2019.1674887

name: Attitude-Social Influence-Efficacy Questionnaire after Bariatric Surgery (ASEQBS)
description: A 28-item questionnaire assessing determinants of dietary adherence among patients after bariatric surgery, based on the attitude-social influence-efficacy (ASE) model. It has four subscales: Intention (4 items), Attitude (7 items), Social Influence (10 items), and Self-Efficacy (7 items). Items are rated on a 1-5 Likert scale; higher subscale scores indicate stronger intention, more positive attitude, more supportive social influence, or greater self-efficacy for dietary adherence.
citation: Wang J, Chen Y, Wang S, Zhang X, Fan Y, Zhang M, Zhu M, Chen H, Wang Y, Kong L, Ni Z (2021). Development and Validation of a Questionnaire to Assess the Determinants of Dietary Adherence Among Patients After Bariatric Surgery. Patient Preference and Adherence, 15, 2865-2875. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S344662

name: Big Five Inventory (BFI-10)
citation: Rammstedt, B., Kemper, C. J., Klein, M. C., Beierlein, C., & Kovaleva, A. (2014). Big Five Inventory (BFI-10). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis76
license: Non-commercial research use only (ZIS standard terms)

name: Big Five Inventory-2
description: A 44-item measure of the Big Five personality traits (Extraversion, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, Neuroticism, Openness) using short trait-descriptive phrases. Items use a 5-point scale (1=disagree strongly to 5=agree strongly). Several items are reverse-scored. Widely used in personality research across cultures. Originally developed in English; Swahili translation from Garrashi et al. (2023).
citation: John, O. P., Donahue, E. M., & Kentle, R. L. (1991). The Big Five Inventory—Versions 4a and 54. University of California, Berkeley, Institute of Personality and Social Research.
license: Non-commercial research use; freely available from Berkeley Personality Lab

name: Big Five Inventory-Short
description: 15-item short measure of the Big Five personality traits (3 items per trait). Scored as mean per dimension on a 1-7 scale.
citation: Lang, F. R., John, D., Ludtke, O., Schupp, J., & Wagner, G. G. (2011). Short assessment of the Big Five: Robust across survey methods except telephone interviewing. Behavior Research Methods, 43(2), 548-567. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-011-0066-z

name: Body Image Concern Scale (BICS)
description: A 24-item self-report measure of body image concern with six subscales: Social Avoidance, Appearance Dissatisfaction, Preoccupation with Reassurance, Perceived Distress/Discrimination, Defect Hiding, and Embarrassment in Public. Items are rated on a 5-point Likert scale; subscale and total scores are sums where higher scores indicate greater body image concern.
citation: He, W., Zheng, Q., Ji, Y., Shen, C., Zhu, Q., & Wang, W. (2017). Development of a Body Image Concern Scale using both exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses in Chinese university students. Neuropsychiatric Disease and Treatment, 13, 1419-1425. https://doi.org/10.2147/NDT.S138762

name: Breast Cancer Survivors Symptom Checklist (BCS-SC)
description: A 14-item self-report checklist for breast cancer survivors, developed to structure follow-up consultations. Thirteen symptom/burden items (fatigue, pain, sleep, body image, menopausal problems, sexuality, weight gain, lymphedema, cognition, emotional distress, social network, work, finances) plus one global 'how are you feeling today' item, each rated 0 (no ailments/symptoms) to 10 (worst imaginable) over the past week. Used at the item level to flag symptoms for discussion; a summary count totals the items reaching a clinical cut-off (pain >= 4, all other items >= 5).
citation: Schou-Bredal, I., Ekeberg, Ø., & Kåresen, R. (2022). Development of the Breast Cancer Survivors Symptom Checklist for Use in Follow-Up Multidisciplinary Appointments. Patient Related Outcome Measures, 13, 235-245. https://doi.org/10.2147/PROM.S364625

name: Children Atopy Screening Questionnaire (ChAt)
description: A 10-item parent-report Yes/No screening questionnaire to identify atopic children who require further allergological evaluation. Each Yes scores 1 and each No scores 0; the total score ranges 0-10, with higher scores indicating a greater probability of allergy. A total score >2 flags children for further evaluation.
citation: Sacchetti M, Baiardini I, Chini L, Moschese V, Bruscolini A, Lambiase A (2017). Development and preliminary validation of a new screening questionnaire for identifying atopic children. Pediatric Health, Medicine and Therapeutics, 8, 99-105. https://doi.org/10.2147/PHMT.S142271

name: Chronic Pain Cognition Scale (CPCS)
description: A 13-item culture-sensitive measure of pain cognition developed in Chinese-speaking chronic pain patients, comprising four factors: Pain Impact, Losing Face, Helplessness, and Avoidance. Items are rated 1-5 and summed; higher scores indicate greater negative pain cognition.
citation: Wu C-H, et al. (2023). Development of the Chronic Pain Cognition Scale: A Culture-Sensitive Pain Measurement in Chinese. Journal of Pain Research, 16, 3075-3087. https://doi.org/10.2147/JPR.S422197

name: Clinicians' Satisfaction with Clinical Pathway Implementation Scale (CSCPI)
description: A 21-item scale assessing Chinese clinicians' satisfaction with the implementation of Clinical Pathways (CP), across three dimensions: Organization Support (9 items), Process Identity (4 items), and Effect Perception (8 items). Items are rated on a 5-point satisfaction Likert scale; higher scores indicate greater satisfaction.
citation: Li J, Shen K, Hu J, Li X, Liu J, Du Y, Huang K (2021). The Clinicians' Satisfaction with Clinical Pathway Implementation: Preliminary Development of an Assessment Scale in China. Risk Management and Healthcare Policy, 14, 257-266. https://doi.org/10.2147/RMHP.S290565

name: COPD Screening Questionnaire (COPD-Q)
description: A 5-item self-scored screening questionnaire for persistent airflow obstruction (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) developed in a general Japanese population. Items cover age, phlegm production, exertional dyspnea, exertional wheezing, and cumulative smoking (Brinkman index). Each response category has a fixed weighted point value; points are summed (range 0-10). A total score of 4 or more suggests persistent airflow obstruction (sensitivity 71.0%, specificity 70.1%).
citation: Samukawa T, Matsumoto K, Tsukuya G, Kumamoto T, Kirichenko S, Ilkovich M, et al. (2017). Development of a self-scored persistent airflow obstruction screening questionnaire in a general Japanese population: the Hisayama study. International Journal of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, 12, 1469-1481. https://doi.org/10.2147/copd.s130453

name: Coronary Heart Disease Patient-Perceived Exercise Benefits and Barriers Scale (CHD-PEBBS)
description: A 22-item measure of how patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) perceive the benefits of, and barriers to, exercise during cardiac rehabilitation. A 12-item Benefits subscale (physiological indicators, physiological function, quality of life) and a 10-item Barriers subscale (lack of exercise support, poor exercise experience/perception, worrying about adverse consequences). Barrier items are reverse-scored so that a higher total reflects a more positive overall perception of exercise.
citation: Liu, Y., et al. (2025). Development and Validation of the CHD-PEBBS: A Scale to Assess Perceived Exercise Benefits and Barriers in Patients with Coronary Heart Disease. Patient Preference and Adherence, 19, 1-16. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S524436

name: Curiosity of Climate Changes Scale (CCCS)
description: A 15-item unidimensional measure of a person's curiosity about climate change - interest in its sources, consequences, and ways of coping. Items are rated on a 5-point agree scale and summed; higher scores indicate greater curiosity about climate change.
citation: Próchniak, P., & Ossowski, A. (2023). Development and Validation of the Curiosity of Climate Changes Scale. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 16, 4829-4838. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S425867

name: Dietary Intake Motivation Questionnaire for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM-DIMQ)
description: A 31-item questionnaire measuring the motivational determinants of dietary-intake behavior in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), grounded in Protection Motivation Theory. Seven dimensions: threat appraisal (severity, susceptibility, internal reward, external reward) and coping appraisal (response efficacy, self-efficacy, response cost). Higher severity/susceptibility/response-efficacy/self-efficacy and lower internal-reward/external-reward/response-cost indicate stronger protective motivation.
citation: Di, J., Zhu, Q., Wu, L., et al. (2023). Exploring Motivations Regarding Dietary Intake Intentions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Development and Validation of a Questionnaire. Patient Preference and Adherence, 17, 2939-2948. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S434348

name: Elderly Abuse by Family Caregivers among Older Adults on Hemodialysis Questionnaire (EABFC-HD)
description: A 57-item self-report questionnaire assessing elderly abuse perpetrated by family caregivers, as experienced by older adults undergoing hemodialysis. Items span seven subscales: psychological misbehavior, authority deprivation, physical misbehavior, financial misbehavior, being abandoned, caring neglect, and emotional misbehavior. Each item is rated on a 4-point frequency scale (1 = never to 4 = always) and summed; higher total scores indicate more severe abuse (range 57-228).
citation: Mahmoudian A, Torabi Chafjiri R, Alipour A, Shamsalinia A, Ghaffari F (2018). The design and evaluation of psychometric properties for a questionnaire on elderly abuse by family caregivers among older adults on hemodialysis. Clinical Interventions in Aging, 13, 543-552. https://doi.org/10.2147/CIA.S149338

name: Elderly Homesickness Questionnaire (EHQ)
description: A 19-item self-report measure of homesickness in older adults, developed and validated in a Chinese sample. Three subscales: Positive Contact (attachment to and engagement with one's hometown), Refusal to Separate (distress at being away), and Homesickness Behavior (behaviors that maintain a connection to the hometown). Each item is rated on a 5-point agree-disagree scale.
citation: Zhang, Y., et al. (2024). Elderly's Homesickness: Development of Elderly Homesickness Questionnaire. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 17, 1479-1492. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S451960

name: Electronic Patient Engagement Behavior Scale (EPEB)
description: A 15-item measure of the online/digital behaviors through which patients engage with their health care. Four subscales: Disease Information Search, Doctor-Patient Interaction, Social Interaction among Patients, and Disease Self-Monitoring. Items are rated on a 5-point agree scale; higher total scores indicate a higher level of electronic patient engagement.
citation: Hou, J., et al. (2024). A Scale for Measuring Electronic Patient Engagement Behaviors: Development and Validation. Patient Preference and Adherence, 18, 837-849. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S444633

name: Emerging Infectious Diseases Preventive Health Behavior Scale (EID-PHB)
description: A 34-item self-report scale measuring preventive health behaviors against emerging infectious diseases across six factors: Droplet Prevention, Contact Prevention, Airborne Prevention, Bloodborne Prevention, Environmental Prevention, and Psychological Coping. Items are rated on a 5-point Likert scale; higher scores indicate more preventive behavior.
citation: Lee WK, Shin SR (2024). Development of Emerging Infectious Diseases Preventive Health Behavior (EID-PHB) Scale and Validation of the Complex Models. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 17, 449-464. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S446006

name: Employee Voice Intention Scale (EVIS)
description: A 9-item measure of an employee's intention to voice opinions and ideas at work, developed via grounded theory among Chinese enterprises. It has two dimensions: Perceived Desirability (4 items) and Perceived Feasibility (5 items). Items are rated on a 5-point agreement scale; higher scores indicate stronger voice intention.
citation: Wang, Y., Zhu, Z., & Wang, X. (2023). Research on Employee Voice Intention: Conceptualization, Scale Development, and Validation Among Enterprises in China. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 16, 2137-2152. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S414623

name: English Translation of the SJT-TW (Situational Judgment Test – Teamwork)
description: 12-scenario Situational Judgment Test assessing knowledge about teamwork effectiveness. Each scenario describes a work-situation faced by a team or team member and presents four behavioural response options; the respondent selects the single best (most suitable) option. The original German version (Gatzka & Volmer, 2017) additionally asks for the worst option; this English translation pilot asked only for the best option to reduce duration. Scoring against a predefined best/worst key (restricted; available from the authors). Authors propose a single total score; a tentative two-factor structure was reported but the authors recommend computing only a total test score.
citation: Freudenstein, J.-P., Remmert, N., Reznik, N., & Krumm, S. (2020). English Translation of the SJT-TW. Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis285

name: Enteral Nutrition Feeding Problems Questionnaire (ENFPQ)
description: A 12-item caregiver-report questionnaire measuring feeding challenges and nutritional problems associated with long-term enteral nutrition among children with disabilities. Items span four domains: tube-related problems, gastrointestinal problems, nutritional status problems, and feeding challenges faced by caregivers. Each item is rated on a 5-point frequency scale; higher total scores indicate more feeding/nutritional problems.
citation: Zaher S, Ajabnoor SM (2025). Development and Validation of a Questionnaire to Measure Feeding Challenges and Nutritional Problems Associated With Long-Term Enteral Nutrition Among Children With Disabilities. Risk Management and Healthcare Policy, 18, 793-803. https://doi.org/10.2147/RMHP.S502223

name: Facial Line Distress Scale-Glabellar Lines (FINE-GL)
description: A 20-item patient-reported outcome measure of the severity of, and distress caused by, glabellar (frown) lines. Two domains: Appraisal of GL (12 items: General, Facial Expression, Certain Situations) and Distress Due to GL (8 items: Public Self-Consciousness, Psychosocial Distress). Each item rated 1-5; higher scores indicate greater glabellar-line severity and distress.
citation: Kang D, Kang E, Choi K, et al. (2025). Development and Validation of Facial Line Distress Scale-Glabellar Lines (FINE-GL). Patient Preference and Adherence, 19, 419-429. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S497415

name: Family Doctor Contracting Services Utilization Willingness Scale (FDCSUW)
description: A 14-item scale measuring willingness to utilize primary care (family doctor contracting) services in China across three dimensions: Perceived Feasibility, Perceived Desirability, and Perceived Initiative. Each item is rated on a 5-point Likert scale; higher scores indicate greater willingness to utilize primary care services.
citation: Li Z, Ma Z (2023). Construction and Scale Development of Willingness to Utilize Primary Care Services: A Study from China. Risk Management and Healthcare Policy, 16, 2171-2185. https://doi.org/10.2147/RMHP.S428369

name: Family Planning Self-Efficacy Scale (FPSES)
description: An 18-item scale measuring a woman's confidence (self-efficacy) in performing family planning activities, developed with rural indigenous women in highland Guatemala. Items span four conceptual subscales (Access, Communication, Social Support, Assertiveness). Each item is rated 1-5 (not at all to completely confident); higher scores indicate greater family planning self-efficacy.
citation: Richardson E, Allison KR, Gesink D, Berry A (2016). Barriers to accessing and using contraception in highland Guatemala: the development of a family planning self-efficacy scale. Open Access Journal of Contraception, 7, 77-87. https://doi.org/10.2147/OAJC.S95674

name: Flourishing Index / Secure Flourishing Index
citation: VanderWeele, T. J. (2017). On the promotion of human flourishing. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 114(31), 8148–8156. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1702996114

name: Flourishing Scale
description: 8-item summary measure of psychological well-being covering social relationships, meaning, purpose, and self-esteem.
citation:
Diener, E., Wirtz, D., Tov, W., Kim-Prieto, C., Choi, D., Oishi, S., & Biswas-Diener, R. (2010). New well-being measures: Short scales to assess flourishing and positive and negative feelings. Social Indicators Research, 97(2), 143–156. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11205-009-9493-y

Arabic translation: AL-Dossary, S. A. (2021). Psychometric properties and measurement invariance of the Arabic version of the Flourishing Scale. International Journal of Psychological Studies, 13(2), 20–27. https://doi.org/10.5539/ijps.v13n2p20

name: Frailty Assessment and Screening Tool (FAST)
description: A 14-item frailty screening instrument covering 10 domains (nutrition, memory, mobility, functional status, mood, physical performance, general health, medication/multimorbidity, continence, and pain), developed and validated for older Indians. Each item is scored 1 (frailty indicator present) or 0 (absent), summed to a total of 0-14; higher scores indicate greater frailty. Cut-offs: pre-frail >=5/14, frail >=7/14.
citation: Gupta P, Mani K, Rai SK, Nongkynrih B, Gupta SK (2021). Development and Psychometric Validation of a New Scale for Assessment and Screening of Frailty Among Older Indians. Clinical Interventions in Aging, 16, 505-516. https://doi.org/10.2147/CIA.S292969

name: General Life Satisfaction Short Scale (L-1)
description: Single-item ultra-short scale measuring general (global) life satisfaction. The respondent rates overall satisfaction with their life on an 11-point rating scale (0-10). The scale score equals the respondent's answer to the one item. English-language adaptation (validated in the United Kingdom) of the German source instrument by Beierlein, Kovaleva, Laszlo, et al. (2015).
citation: Nießen, D., Groskurth, K., Rammstedt, B., & Lechner, C. M. (2021). General Life Satisfaction Short Scale (L-1). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis284

name: General Self-Efficacy Short Scale-3 (GSE-3)
description: 3-item English-language adaptation of the German ASKU (Allgemeine Selbstwirksamkeit Kurzskala) measuring general self-efficacy: the generalized belief in one's competence to cope with a broad range of demanding or novel situations. All three items are positively keyed (no reverse items) and load on a single dimension. Answered on a fully labelled 5-point apply scale; the score is the unweighted mean of the three items.
citation: Doll, E. S., Nießen, D., Schmidt, I., Rammstedt, B., & Lechner, C. M. (2021). General Self-Efficacy Short Scale-3 (GSE-3). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis294

name: Gratitude Questionnaire-6
description: 6-item scale measuring dispositional gratitude — the tendency to notice and appreciate the positive in life. One of the most widely used gratitude measures.
citation: McCullough, M. E., Emmons, R. A., & Tsang, J. A. (2002). The grateful disposition: A conceptual and empirical topography. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 82(1), 112–127. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.82.1.112

name: Hanyang Pain Scale (HPS)
description: A single-item graphic pain rating scale for musculoskeletal pain. Respondents mark one point on an 11-level (0-10) vertical bar, where each level is labeled with a concrete descriptor combining pain frequency, work interference, and sleep disturbance. The score is the marked value (0 = No pain, 10 = Worst possible pain); higher = more severe pain.
citation: Oh, K. Y. (2016). Validation of the Hanyang Pain Scale for clerical workers with musculoskeletal pain. Journal of Pain Research, 9, 207-213. https://doi.org/10.2147/JPR.S102778

name: Health Behavior and Stages of Change Questionnaire (HBSCQ)
description: A Transtheoretical-Model-based screening questionnaire that classifies a respondent's stage of change (pre-contemplation, contemplation, preparation, action, maintenance, relapse, termination) for five cancer-relevant health behaviors: smoking, alcohol consumption, nutritional consultation, physical activity, and use of mammography/ultrasound. It is not a summed scale; each behavior is a single-select item whose chosen option identifies the respondent's current stage.
citation: Gonzalez-Ramirez LP, De la Roca-Chiapas JM, Colunga-Rodriguez C, et al. (2017). Validation of Health Behavior and Stages of Change Questionnaire. Breast Cancer: Targets and Therapy, 9, 199-205. https://doi.org/10.2147/BCTT.S129855

name: Highly Sensitive Person Scale - Revised
description: 18-item revised measure of sensory processing sensitivity across six subscales: Overstimulation, Sensitivity to Positive Experiences, Social Sensitivity, Depth of Processing, Emotional Reactivity, and Sensitivity to Details. Items use a 7-point scale (1=Not at all to 7=Extremely). An average score greater than 5 indicates a tendency towards high sensitivity.
citation: Pluess, M., Aron, E., Kähkönen, J. E., Lionetti, F., Huang, Y., Tillmann, T., Greven, C., & Aron, A. (2024). Evolution of the Concept of Sensitivity and its Measurement: The Highly Sensitive Person Scale-Revised. PsyArXiv. https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/w7bqu. Note: This is a preprint; check https://sensitivityresearch.com/ or https://hsperson.com/ for the published article citation after mid-2025.
license: © Pluess et al. 2024. Permission granted to reproduce for personal, clinical, educational, and research purposes with citation. Unauthorized modifications prohibited. Contact m.pluess@surrey.ac.uk for other uses.

name: Humanistic Professional Awareness Scale for Healthcare Students and Providers (HPAS-HSP)
description: A 20-item scale assessing humanistic professional awareness in healthcare students and providers across three dimensions: Personal Integrity and Accountability, Sensitivity to Others, and Medical Professional Competence. Each item is rated on a 9-point agreement scale; higher scores indicate stronger humanistic professional awareness.
citation: Liao HC, Huang CY, Wang Y. (2021). Development and Validation of a Scale Measuring Humanistic Professional Awareness for Healthcare Students and Providers. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 14, 3213-3223. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S334471

name: Immunoglobulin Treatment Burden Questionnaire (IgBoT-35)
description: A 34-item patient-reported questionnaire (plus one global item) measuring the burden of immunoglobulin (Ig) treatment in patients with primary immunodeficiencies. Items span eight domains: Time, Organisation and Planning, Leisure and Social, Emotional, Travel, Interpersonal Relationships, Employment and Education, and Consequences of Treatment. Higher scores indicate greater treatment burden.
citation: Jones GL, Vogt KS, Chambers D, Clowes M, Shrimpton A (2020). The Development of a New Questionnaire to Measure the Burden of Immunoglobulin Treatment in Patients with Primary Immunodeficiencies: The IgBoT-35. Patient Preference and Adherence, 14, 1567-1584. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S234669

name: Infection Prevention Behavior Scale of Individuals (IPBS-I)
description: A 12-item self-report scale measuring individual infection prevention behaviors in the general population, based on breaking the chain of infection. Three subscales: Blocking the Pathogen (4 items), Blocking Transmission (5 items), and Improving Immunity (3 items). Each item is rated 1-5; higher scores indicate more frequent infection prevention behavior.
citation: Heo, M.-L., & Jang, Y.-M. (2021). Development and Validation of the Infection Prevention Behavior Scale of Individuals (IPBS-I) for the General Population. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 14, 2791-2802. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S334154

name: Inpatients Experiences Measurement Scale (IEMS)
description: A 20-item self-report scale measuring hospitalized patients' experiences across four factors: Care Quality and Information Provision (9 items), Patient Safety and Dietary Services (5 items), Facility and Comfort Infrastructure (4 items), and Comprehensive Patient Support Services (2 items). Items are rated 1-5 and summed; higher scores indicate more positive inpatient experiences.
citation: Kweon Y-R, Jang K-S, Back M, Lee M (2024). Development and Psychometric Test of the Inpatients Experiences Measurement Scale (IEMS). Patient Preference and Adherence, 18, 1359-1372. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S457746

name: Knowledge and Attitude Towards Medication Error Reporting Questionnaire (KAMER)
description: A 16-item questionnaire for pharmacists measuring perceived knowledge of the causes of medication error (10 items) and attitudes representing barriers to medication error reporting (6 items). Each item is rated on a 5-point agreement scale; scores are summed per subscale, with higher knowledge scores indicating greater awareness of ME causes and higher attitude scores indicating greater barriers to reporting.
citation: Mamat R, Awang SA, Ab Rahman AF (2020). Development and Psychometric Validation of a Questionnaire to Evaluate Knowledge and Attitude Towards Medication Error Reporting Among Pharmacists. Drug, Healthcare and Patient Safety, 12, 95-101. https://doi.org/10.2147/DHPS.S249104

name: Loneliness Automatic Thoughts Questionnaire (LATQ)
description: A 9-item unidimensional measure of intense, negative automatic thoughts about loneliness (the cognitive facet of loneliness). Respondents rate how frequently each thought occurred over the past week on a 5-point scale; item scores are summed, with higher scores indicating more frequent loneliness-related automatic thoughts.
citation: Rose, A. L., Goldberg, J. O., Flett, G. L., Nepon, T., & Besser, A. (2024). Totally All Alone with My Thoughts: Development, Psychometric Properties, and Correlates of the Loneliness Automatic Thoughts Questionnaire. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 17, 1115-1131. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S433211

name: Luxembourg Workplace Mobbing Scale (LWMS)
description: Very brief (5-item) unidimensional instrument assessing workplace mobbing exposure in the general working population. Respondents rate how often difficult situations (criticism, being ignored, meaningless tasks, ridicule, conflict) arise with colleagues or a superior on a 5-point frequency scale. All items positively keyed; higher scores reflect greater workplace mobbing exposure. Validated in German, French, and Luxembourgish.
citation: Sischka, P. E., Schmidt, A. F., & Steffgen, G. (2021). Luxembourg Workplace Mobbing Scale (LWMS). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis298

name: Main Character Syndrome Scale
description: 10-item self-report measure of main character syndrome (protagonist-centered self-perception) with two facets: Self-Centrality (SC, items 1–5) and Emotional Amplification (EA, items 6–10). Rated on a 5-point agreement scale. Total = sum of all 10 items (range 10–50; higher = stronger MCS tendencies). Subscale sums (each 5–25) are also reported.
citation: Chaaban, S., Kheir, W., & Tohme, P. (2026). Development and validation of the main character syndrome scale (MCS-10): A psychometric investigation among young adults. Acta Psychologica, 270, 107730. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.actpsy.2026.107730

name: Manchester Respiratory-related Sleep Symptoms scale (MaRSS)
description: An 8-item unidimensional patient-reported scale measuring respiratory symptoms that disturb sleep in patients with COPD (breathlessness, cough, sputum, chest tightness, night-time bronchodilator use, and daytime consequences of poor sleep) over the past 7 days. Items are summed for a total score of 0-32; higher scores indicate greater respiratory-related sleep symptom burden.
citation: Khan N, Vestbo J, Garrow A, et al. (2018). The Manchester Respiratory-related Sleep Symptoms scale for patients with COPD: development and validation. International Journal of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, 13, 3885-3894. https://doi.org/10.2147/COPD.S171140

name: Medicines Use Review Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire (MUR-PSQ)
description: A 12-item questionnaire measuring patient satisfaction with the community pharmacy Medicines Use Review (MUR) service. Two subscales: Experiencing the Service (7 items) and Judging the Service (5 items). All items positively worded on a 5-point agreement scale; higher scores indicate greater satisfaction.
citation: Hindi AMK, Parkhurst C, Rashidi Y, Ho SY, Patel N, Donyai P (2017). Development and utilization of the Medicines Use Review patient satisfaction questionnaire. Patient Preference and Adherence, 11, 1797-1806. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S146991

name: Moral Development Scale for Professionals (MDSP)
description: A 12-item self-report instrument developed in a Scandinavian context and based on Kohlberg's theory of moral development. Items span conventional (stages 3-4) and postconventional (stages 5-6) moral reasoning. Scored as a total sum (12-60); higher scores indicate a higher degree of moral development.
citation: Soderhamn O, Bjornestad JO, Skisland A, Cliffordson C (2011). Construct validity of the Moral Development Scale for Professionals (MDSP). Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 4, 165-170. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S20075

name: Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support
description: 12-item self-report measure of perceived social support from three sources: Significant Other (items 1,2,5,10), Family (items 3,4,8,11), and Friends (items 6,7,9,12). Uses a 7-point Likert scale (1=Very Strongly Disagree to 7=Very Strongly Agree). Scoring is the mean per subscale and mean of all 12 items for the total scale. Widely validated across cultures and languages.
citation: Zimet, G. D., Dahlem, N. W., Zimet, S. G., & Farley, G. K. (1988). The Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. Journal of Personality Assessment, 52(1), 30–41.
license: Free for research and professional use with attribution; not open-licensed

name: Needle Stick Injury Prevention Beliefs Scale (NSI-PBS)
description: A 25-item scale grounded in the Health Belief Model measuring nurses' and healthcare workers' beliefs about needle stick injury (NSI) prevention across six dimensions: Perceived Susceptibility, Perceived Severity, Perceived Benefits, Perceived Barriers, Cues to Action, and Self-Efficacy. Items are rated on a 5-point agreement scale; each subscale is summed, with higher scores indicating stronger endorsement of that construct.
citation: Khraisat FS, Jarrar M, Issa MR, Al-Bsheish M, Hannan J, Aljabri MM, Rayani AM (2026). Development and Validation of the Needle Stick Injury Prevention Beliefs Scale (NSI-PBS) Based on the Health Belief Model (HBM). Risk Management and Healthcare Policy, 19, 564522. https://doi.org/10.2147/RMHP.S564522

name: Nurse Occupational Stigma Scale (NOSS)
description: A 16-item scale measuring perceived occupational stigma directed at nurses, across three dimensions: Negative Label (5 items), Nurse-Patient Relationship (6 items), and Devaluation and Discrimination (5 items). Items are rated on a 5-point Likert scale and summed; higher scores indicate greater occupational stigma toward nurses.
citation: Yang L, Zhang S, Leng J, Fan Z, Luo Y (2022). Development of the Nurse Occupational Stigma Scale. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 15, 1627-1636. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S362709

name: Nursing Work Environment Questionnaire (NWE-q)
description: A 27-item self-report questionnaire assessing nurses' perceptions of their work environment across three dimensions (Nursing Arrangement Rules, Nursing Skill Activities, Nursing Insight), each with System, Organizational, and Individual level items. Rated on a 7-point scale; higher scores indicate a more positive work environment. Scored by summing items per dimension and overall.
citation: Vitale E, Chang Y-C (2024). Validation and Measurement of Psychometric Properties of the "Nursing Work Environment Questionnaire" (NWE-q) in Italian Nurses. Risk Management and Healthcare Policy, 17, 233-247. https://doi.org/10.2147/RMHP.S448083

name: Organizational Commitment Scale (ISSP)
description: 3-item measure of organizational commitment (OC) used in the work-orientations module of the International Social Survey Programme (ISSP). Items assess willingness to exert effort for one's firm/organization, pride in the organization, and willingness to forgo a better-paid job to stay. All items positively keyed. 5-point agree-disagree Likert scale; the recommended score is the unweighted mean of the three items after inverting them so higher scores indicate higher organizational commitment.
citation: Urban, J., Groskurth, K., & Schmidt, I. (2023). Organizational Commitment Scale (ISSP). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis312

name: Outpatient Clinical Teaching Evaluation Questionnaire (OCTE)
description: A 10-item questionnaire evaluating the quality of clinical teaching for undergraduate medical students in outpatient (ambulatory) settings, organized into three subscales: Preparation, Scheduling, and Implementation. Items are rated on a 5-point frequency scale; higher scores indicate better clinical teaching practices.
citation: Baradaran Binazir M, Barzegar M, Heidari F (2020). Psychometric Properties of the Persian Questionnaire for Evaluation of Clinical Teaching at Outpatient Settings. Advances in Medical Education and Practice, 11, 549-555. https://doi.org/10.2147/AMEP.S261350

name: Panic Response Scale (PRS)
description: A 21-item scale measuring panic response during the COVID-19 pandemic across four subscales: Physical Discomfort (7 items), Anxious Fluster (5 items), Sensitive Depression (5 items), and Excessive Prevention (4 items). Each item is rated on a 5-point Likert scale; higher scores indicate stronger panic response.
citation: Tan Y, Lin X, Chen H, Xu M, Tang Y, Gao P, Ren W, Zhang D (2023). Development of the Panic Response Scale and the Predicting Factors of Panic Response During the COVID-19 Pandemic. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 16, 2883-2895. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S415240

name: Partisan Identity Scale (PIS)
description: 8-item English-language scale measuring partisan identity strength: the degree to which a voter identifies with a political party. Adapted from the Identification with a Psychological Group (IDPG) scale (Mael & Tetrick, 1992), it captures a subjective sense of group belonging, the affective importance of party membership, and the affective consequences of lowered group status. The party the respondent identifies with is inserted into each item. All items are positively keyed (no reverse items). A 4-item short form (items 3, 6, 7, 8) is available. The scale targets partisans only and is not meaningful for respondents with no party attachment.
citation: Bankert, A. & Huddy, L. (2019). Partisan Identity Scale (PIS). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis270

name: Patients' Literacy Scale (PLS)
description: A 15-item self-report scale measuring patients' literacy (the ability to obtain, read, and analyze health-related materials, make appropriate decisions, and reduce health-related risks) across four dimensions: Knowledge, Attitude, Practice, and Patient Activation. Items are rated on a 5-point Likert scale; higher summed/mean scores indicate greater patients' literacy.
citation: Jiang D, Sang T, Xiao X, et al. (2022). Development and Initial Validity of the Patients' Literacy Scale Among Outpatients in Hangzhou City, China. Patient Preference and Adherence, 16, 2483-2496. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S379259

name: Patients' Trust in Pharmacists Scale (Singapore)
description: A 12-item scale measuring patients' trust in pharmacists, with three subscales: Benevolence (6 items), Technical Competence (2 items), and Global Trust (4 items). Items are rated on a 7-point scale (-3 to +3) and summed; higher scores indicate greater trust.
citation: Zhang X-H, Jin J, Ngorsuraches S, Li S-C (2009). Development and validation of a scale to measure patients' trust in pharmacists in Singapore. Patient Preference and Adherence, 3, 1-7. https://doi.org/10.2147/ppa.s4362

name: Peer Relationship Scale for Chinese Community-Dwelling Elderly (PRS)
description: A two-part measure of peer relationships in community-dwelling older adults. The PRS-Quantity part (10 items, 6-point) captures the number/frequency of intimate and non-intimate peer relationships; the PRS-Quality part (12 items, 5-point Likert) captures cognitive, affective, and behavioral processes of peer-relationship quality. Higher scores indicate more/better peer relationships (negatively worded affective-process items are reverse-scored in the quality total).
citation: Fu J, Cheng Z, Liu S, Hu Z, Zhong Z, Luo Y (2021). Development and Validation of Peer Relationship Scale for Chinese Community-Dwelling Elderly. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 14, 889-903. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S311352

name: Personal Suffering Assessment
citation: VanderWeele, T. J. (2019). Suffering and response: Directions in empirical research. Social Science & Medicine, 224, 58–66. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2019.01.041

name: Personality Inventory for DSM-5 Brief Form
description: 25-item brief self-report measure of the DSM-5 maladaptive personality trait model, covering five broad domains: Negative Affect, Detachment, Antagonism, Disinhibition, and Psychoticism. Each domain is assessed with 5 items scored 0–3.
citation: Krueger, R. F., Derringer, J., Markon, K. E., Watson, D., & Skodol, A. E. (2012). Initial construction of a maladaptive personality trait model and inventory for DSM-5. Psychological Medicine, 42(9), 1879–1890. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0033291711002674

name: Positive Self-Relation Scale (PSRS)
description: A 16-item self-report measure of a positive relationship to oneself, with four subscales: Self-Confidence, Authenticity and Assertiveness, Self-Acceptance, and Fulfilled Experience. Items are rated 0-10 and summed (three items reverse-scored); higher total = more positive self-relation. Range 0-160.
citation: Ociskova, M., Prasko, J., & Kupka, M. (2019). Positive Self-Relation Scale - development and psychometric properties. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 12, 885-895. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S212923

name: Post Pandemic-Health Promotion Behavior Scale (PP-HPB)
description: A 27-item self-report measure of health promotion behavior among young adults in the post-pandemic digital era, comprising six factors: emotional and social health, personal hygiene, dietary habits, health management, using mobile devices, and physical activity. Items are rated on a 5-point Likert scale; higher scores indicate more health-promoting behavior.
citation: Yu M, Cho SK, Kim SR (2023). Development and Validation of a Scale Measuring the Post Pandemic-Health Promotion Behavior (PP-HPB) of Young Adults in the Digital Era. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 16, 2487-2500. https://doi.org/10.2147/jmdh.s421060

name: Postoperative Recovery Scale for Adult (PRSA)
description: A 10-item generic patient-reported measure of recovery after surgery in adults. Each item covers one recovery domain (pain, nausea/vomiting, fatigue, sleep, diet/drinking, elimination, self-care, mood, family life, social life) and is rated on a 0-100 numeric rating scale anchored from worst (0) to best (100) recovery for that domain. Item scores are summed; higher = better postoperative recovery.
citation: Liu, X., et al. (2025). Developing and Validating a Novel Generic Patient-Reported Outcome Measure – Postoperative Recovery Scale for Adult (PRSA): A Prospective Observational Study. Patient Preference and Adherence, 19, 243-253. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S485263

name: Premenstrual Symptoms Questionnaire - Short Form (PSQ-S)
description: A 9-item self-report screening tool for premenstrual symptoms and their functional impact, derived from the 14-item Premenstrual Symptoms Questionnaire (PSQ). Each symptom is rated for severity over the past several menstrual cycles on a 4-point scale. Unidimensional; the total score is the sum of all items (range 9-36), with higher scores indicating more severe premenstrual symptoms. A total of 22 or higher suggests possible premenstrual disorders (PMDs).
citation: Takeda T, Yoshimi K, Inoue F, Odai T, Shiina M, Nagata C, Ikeda Y, Fukushima K, Ito M. Development and Psychometric Testing of a New Short-Form of the Premenstrual Symptoms Questionnaire (PSQ-S). International Journal of Women's Health, 2022, 14, 963-972. https://doi.org/10.2147/IJWH.S369151

name: Probabilistic Medication Adherence Scale (ProMAS)
description: An 18-item self-report scale measuring general medication adherence, developed with Rasch (item-response) methodology. Items are dichotomous (yes/no); the adherent response scores 1 and non-adherent statements are reverse-coded. The sum score ranges 0-18, with higher scores indicating greater adherence.
citation: Kleppe M, Lacroix J, Ham J, Midden C (2015). The development of the ProMAS: a Probabilistic Medication Adherence Scale. Patient Preference and Adherence, 9, 355-367. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S76749

name: Provider Perception of Team Effectiveness Questionnaire (Provider-PTE)
description: A self-report questionnaire measuring healthcare providers' perceptions of inter-professional team functioning and beliefs about team effectiveness. Twenty-six scored items are grouped into team-process subscales (role clarity, boundary work/trust, team meeting, decision-making, communication, coordination, cohesion, problem-solving, patient-family focus), a belief-about-team-effectiveness item, and an outcomes subscale. Items are rated 1-6; dimension scores are means, with higher scores indicating better team functioning. Three negatively worded items are reverse scored.
citation: Kilpatrick K, Paquette L, Bird M, Jabbour M, Carter N, Tchouaket E (2019). Team Functioning And Beliefs About Team Effectiveness In Inter-Professional Teams: Questionnaire Development And Validation. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 12, 827-839. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S218540

name: Quadrangular Love Scale
description: 40-item self-report measure of love across four dimensions: Compassion (items 1–10), Affection (items 11–20), Closeness (items 21–30), and Commitment (items 31–40). Each subscale contains 10 items rated on a 7-point Likert scale. Compassion and Affection reflect feelings toward the partner; Closeness and Commitment reflect feelings about the relationship. Validated in US and UK samples with high internal consistency (α = .86–.93 per subscale). Items are presented in random order; researcher-only facet labels are not shown to participants.
citation: Karandashev, V., & Evans, N. D. (2019). Quadrangular love theory and scale: Validation and psychometric investigation. Journal of Methods and Measurement in the Social Sciences, 10(1), 1–35. https://doi.org/10.2458/v10i1.23520

name: Resident Healthcare-Seeking Culture Scale (RHCS)
description: A 20-item self-report scale measuring the reasonableness of residents' healthcare-seeking culture across five dimensions: social norms, healthcare-seeking behaviour, personal values, attitudes towards doctors, and perceptions of traditional and modern medicine. Items are rated on a 5-point agreement scale; the total is the mean of all 20 items after reverse-scoring three items, with higher scores indicating a more reasonable healthcare-seeking culture.
citation: Xu H, Feng J, Qiu L, Yan S, Li L, Tian Q, He Y, Lu Z. (2024). Development and Validation of the Resident Healthcare-Seeking Culture Scale (RHCS) Among Chinese Demographics in the Community Setting. Risk Management and Healthcare Policy, 17, 3147-3162. https://doi.org/10.2147/RMHP.S462808

dimensions.name: Perceptions of Traditional and Modern Medicine

name: Respiratory Infection Prevention and Control Self-Efficacy Scale for Adults (R-PACS)
description: A 16-item measure of an adult's self-efficacy for preventing and controlling the spread of respiratory infections. Four subscales: Environmental Management, Contact Restrictions, General Infection Prevention and Control, and Early Detection. Each item is rated on a 5-point agree scale; items are summed (range 16-80), with higher scores indicating greater self-efficacy.
citation: Yoo, H., & Kim, N. (2024). Development of Respiratory Infection Prevention and Control Self-Efficacy Scale for Adults. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 17, 1941-1953. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S456939

name: Risk Proneness Short Scale (R-1)
description: Single-item ultra-short scale measuring the psychological disposition of risk proneness (general willingness to take risks). The respondent rates how willing they are in general to take risks on a 7-point rating scale with labeled endpoints (1-7). The scale score equals the respondent's answer to the one item. English-language adaptation (validated in the United Kingdom) of the German source instrument by Beierlein, Kovaleva, Kemper, et al. (2015).
citation: Nießen, D., Groskurth, K., Rammstedt, B., & Lechner, C. M. (2022). Risk Proneness Short Scale (R-1). Zusammenstellung sozialwissenschaftlicher Items und Skalen (ZIS). https://doi.org/10.6102/zis286

name: Satisfaction of Treatment among Caregivers of Dependent Type 2 diabetic patients (STCD2)
description: A 7-item questionnaire assessing caregivers' satisfaction with the blood glucose-lowering treatment of the dependent type 2 diabetic patient they care for. This file implements the current-status version (STCD2-a). Items 1-6 use a 5-point satisfaction scale and item 7 asks whether the caregiver would recommend the treatment; higher scores indicate greater satisfaction. An overall satisfaction index is the sum of the seven items (range 7-35).
citation: Garcia-Aparicio J, Herrero-Herrero JI (2015). Development, validation, and administration of a treatment-satisfaction questionnaire for caregivers of dependent type 2 diabetic patients. Clinical Interventions in Aging, 10, 969-977. https://doi.org/10.2147/CIA.S83086

name: Scale of Positive and Negative Experience
description: 12-item scale measuring positive (SPANE-P) and negative (SPANE-N) affect over the past four weeks, yielding an affect balance score (SPANE-B).
citation: Diener, E., Wirtz, D., Tov, W., Kim-Prieto, C., Choi, D., Oishi, S., & Biswas-Diener, R. (2010). New well-being measures: Short scales to assess flourishing and positive and negative feelings. Social Indicators Research, 97(2), 143–156. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11205-009-9493-y

name: Secondary Vocational Students Stigma Scale (SVSSS)
description: A 20-item scale measuring junior high school students' stigma toward secondary vocational students, with three subscales: Labeling (9 items), Social Isolation (7 items), and Devaluation and Discrimination (4 items). Higher summed scores indicate greater stigma.
citation: Wang X, Liu Q, Zhang X, et al. (2022). Development of Junior High School Students to Secondary Vocational Students Stigma Scale. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 15, 2925-2938. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S381069

name: Self-Forgiveness Scale (SFS)
description: A 12-item measure of self-forgiveness developed in a Taiwanese (collectivist) context, with three 4-item subscales: Embodied Awareness, Positive Change, and Wisdom Growth. Items are scored on a 5-point Likert scale; higher scores indicate greater self-forgiveness.
citation: Hsu, H.-P. (2021). The Psychological Meaning of Self-Forgiveness in a Collectivist Context and the Measure Development. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 14, 2059-2074. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S336900

name: Self-Management Questionnaire for Lower Extremity Arterial Disease (LESQ)
description: A 22-item self-report measure of self-management behavior in patients with lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) who have undergone endovascular revascularization. Three domains: Medical management (6 items), Rehabilitation exercise management (4 items), and Daily life management (12 items). Each item is rated on a 5-point scale of how fully the behavior is performed; items are summed to a 22-110 total, higher = better self-management.
citation: Shi, X., Li, M., Wang, H., et al. (2024). Development and Validation of the Self-Management Questionnaire for Patients with Lower Extremity Arterial Disease Who Underwent Endovascular Revascularization. Patient Related Outcome Measures, 15, 335-347. https://doi.org/10.2147/PROM.S493159

name: Self-Regulatory Fatigue Scale (SRF-18)
description: An 18-item self-report measure of self-regulatory fatigue (SRF): reduced capacity to regulate thoughts, emotions, and behavior. Items load on cognitive, emotional, and behavioral components. Scored as a sum (range 18-90) with higher scores indicating greater self-regulatory fatigue; health-favorable items are reverse-scored.
citation: Nes LS, Ehlers SL, Whipple MO, Vincent A (2013). Self-regulatory fatigue in chronic multisymptom illnesses: scale development, fatigue, and self-control. Journal of Pain Research, 6, 181-188. https://doi.org/10.2147/JPR.S40014

name: Self-Stigma Scale for Secondary Vocational Students (SSS-SVS)
description: A 21-item self-report measure of self-stigma among secondary vocational (trade-school) students, developed and validated in China. Three subscales: Negative Trait (stereotyped negative traits attributed to vocational students by others), Self-Devaluation (internalized inferiority/shame), and Loss of Opportunity (expected disadvantage in future prospects). Items are rated on a 5-point scale and summed; higher = greater self-stigma.
citation: Leng, X., et al. (2025). Development and Validation of the Self-Stigma Scale for Secondary Vocational Students. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 18, 1-16. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S500492

name: Sensitivity to Pain Traumatization Scale (SPTS-12)
description: A 12-item self-report measure of sensitivity to pain traumatization, defined as the propensity to develop cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses to pain resembling a traumatic stress reaction. Items are rated 0-4 and summed to a single total score (range 0-48); higher scores indicate greater sensitivity to pain traumatization.
citation: Katz J, Fashler SR, Wicks C, Pagé MG, Roosen KM, Kleiman V, Clarke H (2017). Sensitivity to Pain Traumatization Scale: development, validation, and preliminary findings. Journal of Pain Research, 10, 1297-1316. https://doi.org/10.2147/JPR.S134133

name: Sleeping Pills Receptivity and Involuntariness Scale-6 (SPRIS-6)
description: A 6-item measure of psychological receptivity toward hypnotic (sleep-medication) use in insomnia. Two subscales: Involuntary Nature of Insomnia (belief that sleep is brain-regulated and beyond willpower) and Acceptance of Sleep Medication Use. Each item is rated 0-10; the mean is taken, with higher scores reflecting greater psychological receptivity to sleep medications.
citation: Chung, S., & Shahrier, M. A. (2025). Development of the Sleeping Pills Receptivity and Involuntariness Scale-6. Nature and Science of Sleep, 17, 1-12. https://doi.org/10.2147/NSS.S550404

name: Specialty Training's Organizational Readiness for curriculum Change (STORC)
description: A 43-item questionnaire measuring organizational readiness for change (ORC) in postgraduate medical education across 10 subscales (Pressure to Change, Appropriateness, Necessity to Change, Management Support and Leadership, Staff Culture, The Formal Leader, Involvement, Project Resources, Clarity of Mission and Goals, The Implementation Plan). Items are rated on a 5-point agreement scale; subscale scores are the mean of their items, with higher scores indicating greater readiness for change.
citation: Bank L, Jippes M, Leppink J, Scherpbier AJJA, den Rooyen C, van Luijk SJ, Scheele F (2018). Specialty Training's Organizational Readiness for curriculum Change (STORC): validation of a questionnaire. Advances in Medical Education and Practice, 9, 75-83. https://doi.org/10.2147/AMEP.S146018

name: Supportive Care Needs Scale for Patients with Tuberculosis (SCN-TB)
description: A 25-item self-report scale assessing the supportive care needs of patients with tuberculosis across five domains (physical, psycho-emotional, informational, social, practical), each with 5 items. Items are rated on a 5-point need scale; higher scores reflect a higher level of unmet supportive care need.
citation: Li X, Wang B, Tan D, Li M, Zhang D, Tang C, Cai X, Yan Y, Zhang S, Jin Y (2021). Development and Psychometric Testing of the Supportive Care Needs Scale for Patients with Tuberculosis (SCN-TB). Patient Preference and Adherence, 15, 2267-2278. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S330225

name: Teachers' Time Poverty Scale (TTPS)
description: A 7-item single-factor self-report scale measuring teachers' subjective time poverty (the feeling of having insufficient time across work, skill development, and personal/family life). Scored as the sum or mean of all items on a 5-point Likert scale; higher scores indicate greater time poverty.
citation: Liu T, Yang X, Meng F, Wang Q (2023). Teachers Who are Stuck in Time: Development and Validation of Teachers' Time Poverty Scale. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 16, 2267-2281. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S414132

name: Team Effectiveness Scale for Nursing Units (TES-NU)
description: A 22-item self-report scale measuring perceived team effectiveness in hospital nursing units across five factors: Head Nurse Leadership, Job Satisfaction, Cohesion, Work Performance, and Nurse Competence. All items are positively worded and scored on a 4-point Likert scale; higher scores indicate greater perceived team effectiveness.
citation: Kim SO, Kim EY, et al. (2024). Refinement and Validation of the Team Effectiveness Scale for Nursing Units. Risk Management and Healthcare Policy, 17, 2519-2531. https://doi.org/10.2147/RMHP.S477206

name: Therapeutic Adherence Scale (TAS)
description: A brief 4-item self-report screen for medication non-adherence in older adults with chronic disease, capturing both intentional and non-intentional non-adherence. Each item is answered Yes/No; the number of 'Yes' responses is summed (0-4), with higher scores indicating greater non-adherence.
citation: Iovino, P., et al. (2024). Development and Preliminary Psychometric Testing of a Brief Tool to Assess Medication Adherence in Older Adults (Therapeutic Adherence Scale). Clinical Interventions in Aging, 19, 1765-1772. https://doi.org/10.2147/CIA.S480480

name: Treatment Adherence Questionnaire for Patients with Combat Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (TAQ-CPTSD)
description: A 17-item self-report questionnaire measuring treatment adherence in patients with combat-related PTSD, across three subscales: Maintenance of Treatment, Follow-up and Treatment Contribution, and Purposefulness and Responsibility. Items are rated 1 (not at all) to 5 (always) and summed; higher total scores indicate greater treatment adherence.
citation: Ahmadizadeh M-J, Rezaei M, Lotfi M-S (2019). Development and psychometric evaluation of the Treatment Adherence Questionnaire for Patients with Combat Post-traumatic Stress Disorder. Patient Preference and Adherence, 13, 419-427. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S175353

name: Treatment Adherence Scale for Non-Dialysis Chronic Kidney Disease Patients (TAS-NCKD)
description: A 45-item self-report measure of treatment adherence in non-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients, across five domains: Dietary & Nutritional Treatment, Medication Treatment, Exercise & Physical Activity, Lifestyle Modification, and Self-Monitoring & Follow-Up. Each domain contains knowledge, attitude, and behavior items rated on a 5-point agree scale. Items are summed (range 45-225; three negatively worded medication items reverse-scored); higher = better adherence. A total of 179 was the optimal cut-off for 'good adherence'.
citation: Cui, Y., Li, X., Liu, N., et al. (2026). Development and Validation of the Treatment Adherence Scale for Non-Dialysis Chronic Kidney Disease Patients. Patient Preference and Adherence, 20, 1-18. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S573282

name: Unsupportive Social Interaction Scale for Patients with Diabetes (USIS)
description: A 15-item self-report scale measuring unsupportive social interactions experienced by patients with diabetes, with two subscales: Interference (social obligations that interfere with diabetes management) and Insensitivity (people who are demanding, irritating, or hurtful). Items are rated on a 5-point scale; higher scores indicate more unsupportive interactions.
citation: Baron-Epel O, Heymann AD, Friedman N, Kaplan G (2015). Development of an unsupportive social interaction scale for patients with diabetes. Patient Preference and Adherence, 9, 1033-1041. https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S83403

name: Visual Literacy Scale for Health Students and Professionals (VLS-HSP)
description: A 22-item self-report scale measuring visual literacy in health students and professionals across three subscales: Allegorical Meaning (12 items), Explicit Meaning (4 items), and Symbolic Meaning (6 items). Items are rated on a 9-point scale; higher scores indicate greater visual literacy.
citation: Wang, Y.-H., & Liao, H.-C. (2023). A Scale Development for Visual Literacy on Health Students and Professionals. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare, 16, 3129-3141. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S416196

name: WHO-5 Well-Being Index
description: 5-item measure of subjective well-being over the past 2 weeks. Raw score 0-25; percentage score (0-100) = raw score x 4. Scores of 50 or below suggest low mood warranting further assessment.
citation: Topp, C. W., Ostergaard, S. D., Sondergaard, S., & Bech, P. (2015). The WHO-5 Well-Being Index: A systematic review of the literature. Psychotherapy and Psychosomatics, 84(3), 167-176. https://doi.org/10.1159/000376585

name: Work Information Anxiety Questionnaire (WIAQ)
description: A 9-item measure of anxiety related to receiving and monitoring work-related messages/information, grounded in approach-avoidance conflict theory. Two subscales: Reception Anxiety (distress upon receiving work information) and Missing Out Anxiety (unease about possibly missing work information). Items are rated on a 5-point agree scale; higher scores indicate more severe work information anxiety.
citation: Song, X., et al. (2023). Development and Psychometric Properties of the Work Information Anxiety Questionnaire. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 16, 4531-4544. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S435356

name: Youth Purpose Orientation Scale (YPOS)
description: A 19-item self-report measure of youth life-purpose orientations across four domains: Personal Growth, Social Promotion, Family Well-Being, and Personal Well-Being. Respondents rate how important each life goal is on a 5-point scale; each subscale is scored by summing (or averaging) its items, with higher scores indicating a stronger orientation toward that purpose domain.
citation: Wang, H., Gai, X., & Li, S. (2022). Development and Validation of the Youth Purpose Orientation Scale Among Chinese Sample. Psychology Research and Behavior Management, 15, 3485-3496. https://doi.org/10.2147/PRBM.S377052
